authoredPrompt: This figure places three small sketched graphs side by side, labeled (a), (b), and (c), each showing curves that rise from left to right on an unmarked vertical axis above a horizontal axis whose tip is labeled n; no numeric ticks appear anywhere. Panel (a) carries three curves: the highest is labeled c2 g(n), the lowest c1 g(n), and a third labeled f(n) weaves between them, dipping and crossing near the left edge before settling into the corridor between the other two. A dashed vertical segment drops from that crossing region to a tick on the n axis marked n0, and the expression f(n) = Theta(g(n)) is printed below the plot. Panel (b) has two curves, the upper labeled c g(n) and the lower labeled f(n); f(n) oscillates sharply at small n, meets c g(n) at the dashed line standing over the tick n0, and runs beneath it from there on, with f(n) = O(g(n)) underneath. Panel (c) reverses the roles, putting f(n) above and c g(n) below after they touch at the dashed n0 line, and is captioned f(n) = Omega(g(n)). Read against one another, the three panels turn on where the labeled curve sits relative to the scaled comparison function once n passes n0, giving the geometric intuition behind bounding a function from both sides, from above only, and from below only.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for n0: the dashed threshold moves across each plot and violations to its right are marked, making clear that asymptotic bounds only have to hold after a sufficiently large input size.
- Slider for the constant multiplier on g(n): the c g(n), c1 g(n), or c2 g(n) curves move up and down, making clear how constant factors create the allowed upper, lower, or two-sided bound.
- Toggle between Theta, O, and Omega views: the active panel highlights the permitted region for f(n), making clear the difference between two-sided, upper-only, and lower-only comparison.

discrepancies: The default Θ panel contains a large light-blue shaded admissible region, which is not present in the textbook figure and changes the clean line-only appearance.
The generated O panel shows red violation × marks to the right of n₀, contradicting the source panel, which depicts a valid Big-O relationship after n₀ with no violation markers.
Several labels and captions are too small in the rendered screenshot, and at least one curve label appears clipped/partially visible, making the panels harder to read than the source.
The generated curves only approximate the source shapes; panel (a) in particular lacks the distinctive upper-bound curve shape and relative spacing seen in the reference.
The composition is compressed into the left side of the page because of the large control panel, so the three textbook panels do not visually occupy the full wide layout as in the source.
The added UI/status text and highlight modes introduce explanatory overlays that are absent from the source and make the default state less like a drop-in static replacement.
evaluation.notes: The three asymptotic-relation panels are recognizable, but the default blue shading, red violation marks, cramped layout, and weak label legibility make it a poor static replacement for the clean textbook figure.
action_items: Remove or hide the blue admissible-region shading and red violation marks in the default state so the figure initially matches the line-only source.
Choose default n₀ and constant values so each labeled panel depicts a valid Θ, O, or Ω relationship after n₀, especially eliminating the O-panel violations.
Increase the effective drawing size of the three panels and reposition labels so all curve labels, captions, and n₀ labels are clearly visible and unclipped.
Tune the curve functions and relative spacing to better match the source panel shapes, especially the upper and lower comparison curves in panel (a).
plan_action_items: Revise the interaction plan so explanatory highlights and violation diagnostics are optional overlays, not part of the default textbook-replacement view.
